newsitem.title: USA: Aliant continues to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Aliant continues to cut costs.

text.p: Aliant Communications Inc said Tuesday that it is continuing to take cost-cutting measures and improve service in anticipation of a more competitive business.

"Our efforts to re-engineer operations, cut costs, and improve service to customers are continuing as we prepare for a much more competitive environment," said Frank Hilsabeck, president and chief executive, said in a statement.
Earlier, the company reported operating income of $0.31 a share versus $0.29 last year. Revenues were $68.77 million versus $61.13 million.
The operating results exclude one-time restructuring charges recorded in 1995, including a Voluntary Enhanced Retirement Program.
Of the 330 employees who accepted the program, 86 retired during 1996 and the balance will be leaving in 1997.
At the end of 1996, there were 1,676 employees compared with 1,642 in 1995, as the number working in cellular operations is expanding with customer growth, the company said.

Aliant owns stakes in various cellular operations and the company said its number of subscribers grew proportionately by 34.5 percent to 165,233 at 1996 year-end. This compares with a 1995 year-end total of 122,852.

The number of telephone access lines served by Aliant's landline operations rose to 263,208, up 3.6 percent compared with a year ago. Access minutes of use, an indicator of long-distance calling volume, grew by 7.6 percent in 1996, the company said.

"Our cellular operations continue to produce excellent results and represented approximately one-fourth of our consolidated revenues," Hilsabeck said. "In addition, demand for Internet access and enhanced services is steadily increasing."
